## What "covered" means here

A technique counts as covered when at least one stack product satisfies a NIST 800-53 R5 control that the [CTID NIST 800-53 R5 mapping](https://github.com/center-for-threat-informed-defense/attack-control-framework-mappings) links to it ([`data/vendor_to_technique.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/vendor_to_technique.jsonl), the `vendor_to_control` x `control_to_technique` join). This measures control-mapping availability, not a tested detection or prevention. Mappings that CTID keyed on an ATT&CK id that v19 revoked are carried forward to the live successor through [`superseded_by.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl) (465 of 15,722 edge rows are keyed on a revoked id), so revoked ids are never counted as techniques.

Each product is counted once under one key. Products that the edge data used to list under two keys were folded into one in [`data/vendor_to_control.jsonl`](https://github.com/TeamStarWolf/TeamStarWolf/blob/main/data/vendor_to_control.jsonl): `cyberark` -> `cyberark-pam`; `elastic-siem` -> `elastic-security`; `microsoft-defender-for-o365` -> `microsoft-defender-for-office-365`; `qualys` -> `qualys-vmdr`; `rapid7` -> `rapid7-insightvm`; `splunk-es` -> `splunk-enterprise-security`; `tenable` -> `tenable-io`.

Overall: 462 of the 706 live Enterprise v20.0 techniques and sub-techniques are covered (65.4%); 244 are not.

To recompute: `python scripts/compute_coverage.py` (writes all four files in `scores/`; `--check` exits non-zero if they are stale).

## Why the gaps are where they are

Coverage is derived through NIST controls, so a gap means no stack product satisfies any control mapped to the technique. Of the 244 uncovered techniques, 240 have no CTID NIST 800-53 mapping at all (under their own id or a revoked predecessor), so no product can be credited for them through this join, whatever it actually does. Distribution of mapped controls across the gaps: 0 controls: 240, 1 control: 4.

The gap list is therefore ranked by adversary use rather than by NIST depth (`group_count desc, software_count desc, campaign_count desc, nist_control_depth desc, technique_id`). Priority basis: group_count (the number of ATT&CK groups documented using the technique, from the v19.2 profiles): critical >= 20, high >= 10, medium >= 3, low otherwise. Gaps by priority: critical 24, high 21, medium 71, low 128.

Family figures are uncovered/total techniques in the family (the technique and its sub-techniques).

## How to use this analysis

1. Load the [TeamStarWolf Navigator layers](/navigator/) to see coverage on the matrix.
2. Run `python scripts/compute_coverage.py` after the edge tables change; it rewrites this page and the three JSON files.
3. Treat a gap here as "no mapped control in the stack", then confirm with real detection tests before building a business case.
4. As products are added to `data/vendor_to_control.jsonl`, rebuild the join with `python scripts/build_ctid_edges.py` and re-run this script.
5. Cross-reference [CONTROLS_MAPPING.md](/CONTROLS_MAPPING.md) to see which NIST controls a candidate product would satisfy.
